subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw continue making per-agent filesystem confinement opt-in, or should workspace confinement become the default boundary with an explicit upgrade and exec/sandbox plan?
rationale: The remaining change defines a security boundary and changes default behavior for existing users, while related PRs show competing partial implementations with different compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Define a secure default and migration
options.body: Choose the target default confinement posture, document the upgrade path, and require coverage for filesystem tools plus an explicit exec/process decision.

options.title: Keep opt-in confinement
options.body: Leave host-wide access as the documented trusted-operator default and close or redirect this only after maintainers explicitly accept that product/security posture.

options.title: Split filesystem and exec tracks
options.body: Land or sponsor a file-tool boundary separately only if the remaining shell-mediated access is tracked and clearly documented as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Define a secure default and migration
recommendation.body: Choose the target default confinement posture, document the upgrade path, and require coverage for filesystem tools plus an explicit exec/process decision.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest signal from related filesystem-policy reviews and prior workspaceOnly/exec boundary history.
